title: Wu Zetian
summary: Wu Zetian (624-705) entered Emperor Taizong's court, later became empress to his son Gaozong, and held power at court after his death. In 690 she proclaimed herself emperor, replacing the Tang with her own Zhou dynasty, and remained the only woman to rule China in her own right until a court coup removed her around 705.

uncertainty.note: Life span 624-705. Her reign is given as 690-705 by the Ohio State article and 690-704 by World History Encyclopedia.

where.modern_name: Longmen Grottoes, south of Luoyang, Henan, China (site of the Fengxian Cave she commissioned; not her birthplace)
where.historical_name: Longmen, near Luoyang, Tang China (site of the Fengxian Cave she commissioned)

importance.justification: The only woman to rule China in her own right; her reign briefly replaced the Tang with the Zhou dynasty.

sources.title: Wu Zetian: The Only Woman Emperor in Chinese History
sources.author: Victor Xiong

reviewer_note: The pin marks Longmen (her Fengxian Cave), because neither opened source gives a birthplace I could place without assumption; the sources also differ on the end of her reign (704 vs 705).
